held.reason: Fantasy dystopia (book-banning king + sorcerer, Meerkat Press); orwellianesque is SF-side and explicitly not a leftover bin. No fantasy-dystopia thread yet - near-trunk question for the curator.

held.title: Major Arcana
held.author: John Pistelli
held.reason: About-ness fails the marvelous: campus/comics novel with magic-realist seasoning (PW). Candidate not-SFF exclusion question - the curator's ruling, per the exclusion protocol.

held.title: Model Home
held.author: Rivers Solomon
held.reason: Mechanism unresolved: contemporary-haunted-house is split by haunting mechanism (housebound / feral house / residual haunting) and the reviews stress designed ambiguity - Kirkus: the siblings 'can't agree whether their parents were killed by supernatural forces'; Reactor's review is literally titled 'Is the House What's Haunted?'; Locus: the house is 'cursed and malignant' (a malign agent would break feral-house's not-evil clause; no specific dead person verified for housebound; a dark presence contradicts residual's no-agent). Needs a mechanism-establishing source or the curator's ear.

held.title: Moderation
held.author: Elaine Castillo
held.reason: About-ness fails the speculative engine test: Locus (Niall Harrison): 'the romance is in the foreground, which means the science fiction is in the background'; contemporary tech-industry novel with VR worlds as setting, not engine. Candidate not-SFF exclusion question - the curator's ruling.

held.title: Mothtown
held.author: Caroline Hardaker
held.reason: Register unverified: transformation/becoming tale with missing people and a door-world package; nearest leaf metamorphic-magic-realism sits at 9, so a freeze-triggering placement needs a solid mechanism read first. Reviews stress the book "begs not to be defined".

held.title: Never Flinch
held.author: Stephen King
held.reason: Not-SFF exclusion question: King's own blurb is a pure crime thriller (threat letter, stalker, bodyguard Holly Gibney) with zero supernatural content.

held.title: Night Swimming
held.author: Aaron Starmer
held.reason: About-ness: a 90s summer romance whose speculative element is one unearthly twist at a hidden pool ("one unearthly twist", "plays with the boundaries of reality") - seasoning, not engine, on current evidence.

held.title: North Sun, Or The Voyage of the Whaleship Esther
held.author: Ethan Rutherford
held.reason: About-ness + nature unverified: PW grounds a harsh 1878 whaling novel with one supernatural presence (a seabird-man spirit, Old Sorrel, haunting the crew) - single spirit in a literary historical; whether the haunting is engine or seasoning unclear.

held.title: Nothing in the Basement
held.author: Romie Stott
held.reason: Mechanism ambiguous: domestic water-attacks (bathtub near-drowning, sewage) plus a repeated denial refrain "There is nothing in the basement" - feral house (house as agent) vs a denied presence (which would need a specific dead person for housebound). Blurb does not resolve it.

held.title: Shadow Ticket
held.author: Thomas Pynchon
held.reason: About-ness unverified: 1930s Milwaukee detective novel with 'Hungarian magicians' (WaPo) - stage conjurers or real magic unresolved; the speculative engine is unproven. Needs one more source or the curator's ear.

held.title: Singer Distance
held.author: Ethan Chatagnier
held.reason: No clean leaf: literary SF of ESTABLISHED Mars communication (messages since 1894, alternate-1960 MIT setting, Kirkus) - first-contact children do not fit (not first, not outward voyage, not far/near-future); not alt-history (world untransformed). Serve-shape for the curator.

held.title: Sundial
held.author: Catriona Ward
held.reason: About-ness gate: LJ/PW call it horror with science-fiction elements (family behavior experiments in the Mojave; Horror Bound tags supernatural) but the marvelous may be marginal - the engine reads as psychological family horror. Both sides: Carpe Librum says it introduces a level of SF; PW genre-tags Sci-Fi/Fantasy/Horror. Held for the curator's ear, no lean.

standing_rules.name: Absurd Shit rule
standing_rules.source: the curator: "I'm making an 'Absurd Shit'-rule: if it's too absurd to say if it's SF or Fantasy, and it's not even a Fabulation: kill it"
standing_rules.apply: Autonomous, no per-case ask: if a book is too absurd to call SF or Fantasy AND fits no Fabulation node, exclude as not SFF. Log each kill in sweep.log as '-Title (Absurd Shit rule)' and in excluded[] with reason citing the rule.
